name: Question 15
problem: The coefficient of ${x}^{7}{y}^{3}$ in the expansion of ${(x+7y)}^{10}$ is
worked_solution:
The binomial theorem states that for any positive integer $n,$ we have

$$
(a+b)^{n}=(\frac{n}{0}){a}^{n}{b}^{0}+(\frac{n}{1}){a}^{n-1}{b}^{1}+(\frac{n}{2}){a}^{n-2}{b}^{2}+…+(\frac{n}{n}){a}^{0}{b}^{n}.
$$

In the case of ${(x+7y)}^{10},$ we have $a=x,$ $b=7y,$ and $n=10.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{(x+7y)}^{10}=(\frac{10}{0}){x}^{10}(7y)^{0}+(\frac{10}{1}){x}^{10-1}(7y)^{1}+(\frac{10}{2}){x}^{10-2}(7y)^{2}+⋯+(\frac{10}{10}){x}^{10-10}(7y)^{10}.\end{aligned}
$$

From here, we see that the ${x}^{7}{y}^{3}$ term must be

$$
(\frac{10}{3}){x}^{10-3}(7y)^{3}.
$$

Simplifying this term, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(\frac{10}{3}){x}^{10-3}(7y)^{3} & =120{x}^{7}\cdot {7}^{3}{y}^{3} \\  & =120{x}^{7}\cdot 343{y}^{3} \\  & =41\,160{x}^{7}{y}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coefficient of ${x}^{7}{y}^{3}$ is $41\,160.$

EXPLANATION

The binomial theorem states that for any positive integer n, we have (a+b)n=(n0)anb0+(n1)an−1b1+(n2)an−2b2+…+(nn)a0bn.

In the case of (x+7y)10, we have a=x, b=7y, and n=10. Therefore, (x+7y)10=(100)x10(7y)0+(101)x10−1(7y)1+(102)x10−2(7y)2+⋯+(1010)x10−10(7y)10.

From here, we see that the x7y3 term must be (103)x10−3(7y)3.

Simplifying this term, we get (103)x10−3(7y)3=120x7⋅73y3=120x7⋅343y3=41160x7y3.

Therefore, the coefficient of x7y3 is 41160.
